title: Notes must agree at the joins.
body: Each chapter note is a card on one line. Wherever two cards cover the same idea, a seam joins them. It is read from both sides, and it glows when they disagree. · symbols: whale, line, seam, atom, pod

title: Give each note its own card.
body: Notes are cards of different heights instead of one flat pile. Neighbours are compared only on the part they share, so a wrong link shows up as a visible gap. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, ring

title: Keep the red join red.
body: Team reports are lines that meet at joins. Each join carries a traffic light that is set by reading both sides, and paint will not stick to it. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pod

title: Map the joins, then merge.
body: A folder is a row of cards tied by threads. Mapping draws every thread as a checked join before anything moves, so a thread with no far end is caught on the map. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, flag

title: Show both sides of the edge.
body: Two sources are two lines that meet at a join. Instead of throwing one answer into the sea, both cards sit on the join with their labels, and the join glows if they differ. · symbols: whale, line, seam, atom, pod

title: One owner for every join.
body: The plan, data, code and output are four lines that share pieces. Every shared piece is a join with one owner tick and a gate that checks each copy against the owner. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate, tick

title: Seven opinions, one line.
body: Seven pods sit in a ring, each joined to its neighbours. Every beat each nudges toward the others, and the ring settles into one line without a boss. · symbols: whale, line, pod, seam, counter

title: Keep both. Mark the join.
body: Memory is a line of cards. A new card that disagrees with an old one lands beside it, joined by a glowing seam, and a tick goes to a person instead of the old card sinking. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pod, tick

title: Test the gate by breaking it.
body: The checker is a gate. The whale bends cards on purpose and fires them at it, and each bounce earns a tick, so a gate that never stops anything is exposed. · symbols: whale, line, gate, seam, tick

title: Trust the parts that agree.
body: An AI answer is a line of cards. Each card is checked against its neighbours: those that fit go solid, a card that fits nothing stays dashed, and nothing looks sure by default. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, tick

title: Fold only the joins that agree.
body: Each agent's answer is a card on the line. Where two cards meet is a join. Only joins that agree rise into a gold trunk; the rest stay visible below. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: Odd joins wait for a person.
body: A fast line of agent cards. Joins that look odd get set aside on a short side branch with an empty person chip, and they only rejoin after a tick from a reviewer. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, tick

title: Every push meets the gate.
body: Every new card passes a gate right where it lands. The gate's lintel shows the card's outline: if the shape does not fit, the gate closes and a flag goes up. · symbols: whale, line, gate, flag, pod

title: Let every join pull back.
body: The line is a molecule's chain, folded into a knot. Wherever two parts of the chain touch, a join pulls them together; let go, and all the joins pull the knot back into its outline. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pin, ring

title: Floppy parts have fewer joins.
body: Count the joins holding each part of the chain. Parts with many joins barely move; parts with few swing wide. A warm-to-cool wash along the line becomes a wobble map. · symbols: whale, line, seam, ring, pod

title: See every link below the top.
body: The web of projects is laid out in rows: what you fund, what they use, what those use. Links run between rows, so a crack two rows down is traced up to every big card that leans on it. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, flag

title: Credit should flow down the links.
body: Every link down from a card carries a share of its credit, shown as the thickness of the stream. A pin on each card keeps what it passes on below what it got. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pin, tick

title: Draw only links you can show.
body: The whale holds the source document as it draws. A link goes in only where the source shows it; guessed arrows fade. A core box with no outgoing links is left alone, because that is what the source says. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pod, flag

title: Let the unfinished joins glow.
body: Built joins stay teal. Joins the plan names as not built yet glow terracotta with a flag, so pods stop at them instead of falling through. The whole map honestly reads 'not finished'. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pod, flag

title: Rules on top, parts below.
body: The rule cards go on top, pinned. Then the big parts, then what users touch, then what is named as next. Links run only between rows where the docs show them. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pin, pod

title: A wiki with pins.
body: The wiki is a line with dots joined by threads. Three pins hold what must stay true, so the line can bend freely and the threads still land. · symbols: whale, line, pin, pod, tick

title: Merge, and keep the seams.
body: Two team lines are laid side by side. Wherever they meet, a seam shows whether they agree. Disagreements stay visible in one marked box instead of one covering the other. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pod, tick

title: The same mistake, pinned.
body: A mistake found after saving is a flag. It becomes a hollow pin that watches first, then a solid pin once it proves itself, so the same smudge bounces off next time. · symbols: whale, line, pin, flag, tick

title: Don't touch the gate.
body: Gates and pins sit on a heavy base the pod cannot move. Its only path is back to the line, fixing what was named. A law changes only with a signed tick. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod, tick

title: We choose the pins.
body: Upper lane: an evenly spinning ring keeps its amount, so the kept thing follows from the spin. Lower lane: we place pins by hand, and more come from mistakes. The arrows point opposite ways. · symbols: whale, line, pin, ring, flag

title: Try first. Then the gate opens.
body: Each puzzle's answer card sits behind a gate. The whale's own line has to reach the puzzle and leave a tick before the gate opens. · symbols: whale, line, gate, tick

title: Find the pin first.
body: A problem is a tangled line. Turn it and one point never moves. Drop a pin there and the tangle unwinds around it, and the same pin works on every turned copy. · symbols: whale, line, pin, ring

title: Small changes, one counter.
body: Each small bend of the line adds a sliver to one counter bar. When the bar nears its line, the whale stops and asks. · symbols: whale, line, counter, gate, pod

title: AI writes. The gate checks.
body: The AI pod hands over small batches. A gate measures each batch against three pins, the pod fixes what was named, and anything it cannot fix comes to the whale with a flag. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod, flag

title: Two copies, one seam.
body: Doc and build are two rails. Short seams join them at each shared point, and a gate waits until both sides match, so the rails always step together. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate, pod

title: Give every note a label.
body: Notes are cards that all look the same until each gets a coloured tab for its kind; the brief is a tree of sockets that only takes the right kind in each slot. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: Hand over only the right cards.
body: Cards hang from the line in tiers, from rules for everyone down to this one job; a helper standing at its job sees its own tier and the tiers above, never a neighbour's. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pod, seam

title: One fact at every joint.
body: The brief forks into two arms, one per helper; a fact lives once on the trunk and both arms read it through the fork, so a changed copy lights up the fork instead of travelling. · symbols: whale, line, pod, seam, atom

title: Private cards stay home.
body: A brief is a stack of cards on the line; a private card carries a sealed tab, and a send gate at the end of the line only opens for cards that belong to the client receiving the brief. · symbols: whale, line, atom, gate, pod

title: Send the wiring, not the pile.
body: Each file becomes a small card that keeps only its sockets and the wires between them; repeated wiring shapes fold into one pattern card with a key, so the whole map fits where the pile never did. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: Draw the sockets first.
body: Each step is a card with sockets and wires, like a circuit drawing; because the wires say exactly how steps join, joining left-first or right-first gives the same tree, and any branch can be rebuilt alone. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: See every joint first.
body: The codebase is a web of cards hanging from the line; draw every link as an arrow from the part that calls to the part it needs, and the knots and loops stand out like snags in a net. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, flag

title: Add the missing piece.
body: Two cards meet with sockets of different shapes; instead of jamming them, a small two-sided card that fits each side slides between them, a named converter. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: Each helper gets its own part.
body: One document is one line; split it at marked joints into separate stretches, one per helper, and helpers can work at the same moment without touching each other's ink. · symbols: whale, line, pod, seam, tick

title: Find the joint that slipped.
body: Build the same answer twice, once through the parts and once straight from the brief, and lay the two trees side by side; wherever they differ, that joint lights, like comparing two maps of the same street. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: Build it once, with slots.
body: One line drawn once with blank cards hanging on it; each new job only drops its facts into the blanks. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pod

title: Stop when the counter hits zero.
body: Outline whales are fresh readers who ring each kink they find; a counter shows how many; the whale fixes the list and asks again until the counter reads zero. · symbols: whale, line, ring, counter

title: Send only what clears the gate.
body: A gate on the line with a mark on its lintel; a ring scores each line as it arrives; below the mark it goes back for another pass. · symbols: whale, line, gate, ring, counter

title: One line for every puzzle.
body: Instead of a fresh wavering line per card, the whale draws one careful line once, and every card runs along it and comes out ticked. · symbols: whale, line, atom, tick

title: Every try gets a tick.
body: Each new shape of the line drops a tick on a strip below, carrying a tiny copy of the shape and its result, so any tick brings that shape back. · symbols: whale, line, tick, gate

title: A small gate picks the road.
body: A gate at the start rings each line to size it, then sends it down one of three roads: short, branching or looping. · symbols: whale, line, gate, ring, counter

title: Check every join in the chain.
body: Where each step hands to the next there is a seam with a small gate; a wobbly step is stopped and redone at its own seam. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate

title: Keep the judge pinned.
body: Pins lock the gate posts; the whale may reshape only the line; moving a post needs a second whale to sign a tick. · symbols: whale, line, pin, gate, tick

title: One change, then measure.
body: The whale smooths exactly one kink per lap; a ring measures; the counter rises (keep, a tick lands) or falls (the line springs back). · symbols: whale, line, ring, counter, tick

title: Let it draft the cards first.
body: The whale hands the pod its rough line; the pod sends back a stack of tabbed cards (goal, context, check); the whale fixes one and adds its facts. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pod

title: Hunches don't fit the slot.
body: The ship lever sits behind a socket shaped for evidence. A pink guess card bounces off it, and only a green test card snaps in. Only then does the lever move. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, pod

title: When unsure, the gate stays shut.
body: A gate with three lamps sits on the line. It opens only for a clear yes, stays shut on an unsure card, and slams on harm. Shut is its resting state. · symbols: whale, line, gate, atom, pod

title: Every step gets a tick.
body: Each finished step drops a tick on the line. After a crash the whale resumes from the last tick, not the start, and the paying card waits at the very end behind a gate, so it fires once. · symbols: whale, line, tick, gate, atom

title: Doing waits behind the gate.
body: The line splits into three stations: the pod answers small questions about the draft, a gate of plain rules reads the answers, and a tick records the result. The send card stays locked behind the gate until the whale switches it on. · symbols: whale, line, pod, gate, tick

title: Five small gates, not one.
body: The big question card splits along its folds into five small cards. Each passes its own small gate, and the decision is read off five clear lamps instead of one blurry ring. · symbols: whale, line, atom, gate, ring

title: First, check the ruler.
body: Before measuring real work, the whale runs the ring over a pinned card whose answer is already known. Only when the ring reads it right does it touch the real line. · symbols: whale, line, ring, pin, flag

title: Coin flips go to a person.
body: A meter with a shaded middle band sits on the line. Answers inside the band, and any card that moves money, are lifted out to the whale. Only clear answers on small things keep flowing. · symbols: whale, line, ring, gate, atom

title: Leave the flag where it is.
body: Pins above the line are written promises. Where a piece of the line disagrees with its pin, the joint glows copper and a flag is planted and left standing until someone really fixes it. The done lamp stays dark while any flag stands. · symbols: whale, line, pin, seam, flag

title: Every claim faces the same gates.
body: Five small gates stand on the line, each testing one thing (a reusable part, a real leap, a principle, a first, reuse by others). Every card runs the same five, and only those that pass reach a short shelf. · symbols: whale, line, atom, gate, counter

title: Readers pass a one-way gate.
body: The live line gets a read-only twin behind a one-way gate. Readers can see every page, but the gate has no keyhole: a key card bounces off and nothing changes from the reading side. · symbols: whale, line, gate, atom, pod

title: Every miss gets a new gate.
body: Each gate checks one kind of thing, shown as an icon on its lintel. A miss of a new kind passes them all, and its flag becomes the icon of a new gate. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod, flag

title: Add a different gate.
body: A row of identical gates all ask the same question, so the same bug passes them all. Swapping one copy for a gate with a new icon catches it. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod

title: Turn every miss into a gate.
body: The flag that marks a miss is folded into the icon of a new gate, so the next run is checked for that kind of mistake too. · symbols: whale, line, gate, flag, pod

title: The old bug hits a gate.
body: Keep the old bug as a ghost run. Build a gate that stops the ghost before the fix ships, so the bug can never swim back in unnoticed. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod, tick

title: Fresh eyes try to break it.
body: Pods that didn't draw the line try to break it. A poke counts only with a tick of evidence, and a different pod fixes what they find. · symbols: whale, line, pod, tick

title: Check the pin before the work.
body: The pin is the written rule. A gate compares the line with the pin, never with what you meant, so a second gate tests the pin against known answers. · symbols: whale, line, pin, gate, atom

title: Find the first broken joint.
body: An agent's run is a line of steps. A small gate at each joint checks that what one step hands over fits what the next needs, so the first break lights up. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate, pod

title: Show one real example.
body: A claim is a card with a socket for an example. A gate refuses claims whose socket is empty, so every claim arrives with something you can try. · symbols: whale, line, atom, gate, pod

title: Seven gates watch every frame.
body: Seven gates, each with its own icon, watch a film's frames for seven different kinds of flaw, including the film's own whale turning too fast. · symbols: whale, line, gate, pod

title: Check the work, not its label.
body: A label tag rides on each run. A gate that reads the tag passes wrong work. Turning the gate's lens onto the line itself catches it. · symbols: whale, line, gate, atom, pod

title: Every answer keeps its receipt.
body: Every card the pod brings back has a small tick in its corner, and a thin line runs from that tick back to the exact message it came from. Copper alarm. · symbols: whale, line, atom, tick, pod

title: Give every note a label.
body: Every memory card wears a coloured tab that says how sure we are, and the tab can only move up after a fetch tick passes a gate. Rust alarm. · symbols: whale, line, atom, gate, tick

title: Every step leaves a mark.
body: The pod's line leaves a strip of ticks under it, one per step, and a gate after each step lets the line go on only when it glows green. Rust alarm. · symbols: whale, line, tick, gate, pod

title: Draw only the joins you see.
body: The map keeps only the joins found in the source, drawn teal. Planned but unbuilt joins stay on the map in copper, and the pinned base of rules has no false lines drawn out of it. · symbols: whale, line, seam, pin, pod

title: Test where the parts join.
body: The line runs through three parts, and a small gate sits on every join between them. The checks live at the joins, not inside the parts. Raw sienna alarm. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate, pod

title: A gate after every step.
body: A gate stands after every station on the line, and each station hands on only work that has passed its gate. The rules sit as pins that never move. Raw sienna alarm. · symbols: whale, line, gate, tick, pin

title: Let the check only look.
body: A gate splits the checker in two: a reading part inside that only rings the line, and a thin outer layer, behind the gate, that is the only part allowed to touch files. Copper alarm. · symbols: whale, line, gate, ring, counter

title: Some numbers get a pin.
body: Three pins hold the baton line at its weight, light and size. The pod can bend the shape however it likes between them, and any tug on a pin is measured and snapped back. Copper alarm. · symbols: whale, line, pin, ring, pod

title: Start with the small card.
body: The cards stack into four layers on the line: one small summary card on top, then notes, full text, the original. The pod goes down one layer at a time, only as far as it needs. Rust alarm. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pod, ring

title: Three runs, one gate.
body: Three whales build the same line three separate ways from one shared plan card, and the three lines must meet a gate at exactly the same height. Rust alarm. · symbols: whale, line, gate, ring, pod

title: Let the colours ring.
body: Each colour card sends up a ring. The rings stack into one chord above the line, so the whole set is heard at once instead of judged pair by pair. · symbols: whale, line, atom, ring, pod

title: Keep the reading pair pinned.
body: Two pins hold the ink and the paper apart. Every colour set passes a gate that checks ink against paper, so the colours can change while the words stay sharp. · symbols: whale, line, pin, gate, pod

title: Three parts, many songs.
body: Three small typed cards and a short list of moves. Every new sound is a tree of cards snapped at joints that only take the right kind, with a receipt at each joint. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam, tick

title: Finished is when every gate opens.
body: A row of small gates along the line. The line runs through all of them each round. Flags show what failed, and the counter climbs until every gate glows. · symbols: whale, line, gate, flag, counter

title: Shrink it through the gates.
body: Five gates along the line, each smaller than the last. At each one the mark drops one detail by choice, and a ring checks it still reads at tab size. · symbols: whale, line, gate, ring, pod

title: Draw the order as one line.
body: The whale writes the order as one short line of arrows. Pods line up along it, split where steps run side by side, and a gate checks the line before anything runs. · symbols: whale, line, pod, gate

title: Pull every thread into view.
body: The cards lift out of their folders and become points on a sphere, with threads between linked cards. Groups gather, and the card many threads pass through swells. · symbols: whale, line, atom, ring, pod

title: Every shape gets one pin.
body: A shelf above the line holds a few shape cards, each pinned to one word. The whale takes shapes from the shelf instead of drawing, so a circle always means the same thing. · symbols: whale, line, atom, pin, pod

title: Taste, one tick at a time.
body: The pod offers two small cards, and the whale keeps one. Every pick lands as a tick on a strip, and the next pair drifts toward the whale's own lines and colours. · symbols: whale, line, pod, tick, counter

title: Every sound on the tick.
body: Ticks sit on the line at each picture change. Each sound is a ring written onto a tick, so when the edit moves, the ticks move and the rings move with them. · symbols: whale, line, tick, ring, pod

title: Every frame lives on the line.
body: The line is the clock. Each tick on it names one exact picture, so the whale can land on any tick, any number of times, and find the same frame. · symbols: whale, line, tick, gate

title: Every join must hold.
body: A film is a line made of pieces. Where two pieces meet is a join that must line up, and only a line whose joins all match goes out to the pod. · symbols: whale, line, seam, gate, pod

title: Two copies, one card.
body: Script, data, code and screen are four cards on one line. Wherever two repeat the same words is a join, and one owner card at each join is the copy the others follow. · symbols: whale, line, atom, seam

title: Run the ring end to end.
body: A ring is a look at one stretch of the line. Sliding the ring end to end, step by step, turns a peek into a full check. · symbols: whale, line, ring, gate

title: Nothing fake gets past the door.
body: Each package is a card that must pass a door on the line before the pod opens it; the door looks inside, and a hollow card never gets through. · symbols: whale, line, gate, atom, flag

title: Turn each rule into a door.
body: A rule on a scroll is a sign by the road. Torn off and planted on the line, it becomes a door the work has to pass through. · symbols: whale, line, gate, tick

title: The old bug meets a door.
body: Every patch leaves a small door right behind it, cut to the shape of the old kink, so the old copy can never slip back through. · symbols: whale, line, gate, flag

title: Lay the cards side by side.
body: Two answer cards laid side by side under one chip. If the chip reads them the same but they are not the same, that pair shows exactly what the score cannot see. · symbols: whale, line, atom, ring

title: Every version gets a tick.
body: Each finished version gets a tick tied to it by a thread to the tick before; tug any old version and every later thread goes taut. · symbols: whale, line, tick, flag

title: Put a ring on every turn.
body: A ring rides with the whale and measures each turn. A turn that overfills the ring stops the film before it is made. · symbols: whale, line, ring, gate
